title: How Relations Impose Embedding-Space Structure
abstract: arXiv:2611.29986v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are known to encode simple relations, such as synonymy, in the geometry of their representations. It is unclear whether they also encode complex patterns of relationships such as those that drive analogy. We present a simple method, with no learned parameters, based on comparing the internal structural arrangements between disparate domains, to test this. Using our method we find over multiple models that representations are arranged consistently to encode complex relationship similarities. Models align distant representation clouds so that facets of meaning are easily comparable under simple mappings. Our work extends mechanistic accounts of representation space to the relative arrangement of representations that may be only weakly related to one another, showing that representation geometry is far richer than previously thought. Code and data: https://github.com/lcowley7/embedded_relationships

translated_title: 关系如何塑造嵌入空间结构
translated_abstract: 众所周知，语言模型会在其表示的几何结构中编码简单关系，例如同义关系。然而尚不清楚它们是否也编码复杂的关系模式，例如驱动类比推理的那些模式。我们提出了一种简单的方法，无需学习任何参数，基于比较不同领域之间的内部结构排列来对此进行测试。使用该方法，我们在多个模型中发现表示被一致地排列以编码复杂的关系相似性。模型将对齐相距遥远的表示云团，使得意义的各个方面在简单映射下易于比较。我们的工作将表示空间的机制性解释扩展到了可能彼此仅有微弱联系的表示之间的相对排列，表明表示几何结构远比之前认为的更加丰富。代码和数据：https://github.com/lcowley7/embedded_relationships
tldr: 本文提出一种无需学习参数的简单方法，通过比较不同领域间的内部结构排列，发现语言模型的表示被一致地排列以编码复杂的关系相似性，表明表示几何结构远比以往认为的更加丰富。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a simple parameter-free method that compares internal structural arrangements across disparate domains, revealing that language models consistently arrange representations to encode complex relationship similarities, showing that representation geometry is far richer than previously thought.
